title: The Extraction of Geneva
premise: Lena Amberdale, a disgraced analyst blacklisted by three intelligence agencies, is pulled back in when a voiceprint match—her own, recorded years ago—unlocks a black server in Geneva containing proof that a planned defection before a global summit is staged bait. The defector, Marek Voss, is a former colleague she once loved and was ordered to betray, and the extraction is designed to flush out everyone who ever doubted the program that ruined them both. As Lena and Marek run a gauntlet of compromised handlers, mercenary hunters, and the summit's tightening security perimeter, she discovers the true target is not Marek but the server itself and the witnesses it protects. In the end, Lena chooses love against duty: she burns the extraction, broadcasts the archive during the summit's opening session, and walks away with Marek into anonymity while the program's architect falls—not to a bullet, but to exposure.
about_author: Ada Nystrom is a former policy researcher who spent a decade inside European security institutions before leaving to write fiction full-time. She lives between Copenhagen and Lisbon, where she writes thrillers about the human cost of systems that mistake people for assets.

chapters.title: The Voice That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Working dead-end contract audits in Riga, Lena receives an automated alert: her voiceprint, recorded fifteen years ago, just unlocked a server in Geneva. She never authorized it. The beat is cold dread—the past knocking with her own voice.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Three Exits
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, POV Lena. We learn how she was burned: scapegoated at each agency for failures she flagged in advance. Emotional beat: the slow erosion of belief in institutions, ending with her decision to fly to Geneva anyway.

chapters.title: Server Nine
chapters.summary: POV Lena. In a Geneva data vault, she accesses the server and finds an extraction dossier: Marek Voss, defector, summit week, dead-drop schedule. And a flag: ASSET LIKELY COMPROMISED—BAIT PROBABLE. Beat: recognition and fear.

chapters.title: The Man in the Photograph
chapters.summary: POV Marek. In a safehouse outside Lyon, Marek prepares his defection, unaware he's being managed. He keeps a photo of Lena. Beat: tenderness shadowed by the sense he's being watched by people he trusts.

chapters.title: Handler with Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Lena. She contacts her old handler, Aldous Renner, now a summit security consultant, who warns her off with genuine warmth and a genuine threat. Beat: the seduction of being wanted back.

chapters.title: The Bait Doctrine
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Marek's handlers move up his extraction timeline; he notices the route passes through a kill-box he helped design years ago. Beat: dawning suspicion that his defection is theater.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Dead Language
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Following the dossier's drop schedule, Lena intercepts a courier and finds a second message hidden in cipher only Marek would use: DON'T TRUST THE PLAN. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Renner's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Renner. Renner reports Lena's movements to Program Director Ilse Karrigan, but keeps his own private copy of the server's index. Beat: a loyal man beginning to hedge.

chapters.title: Lyon, Before Dawn
chapters.summary: POV both, alternating. Lena reaches Marek's safehouse minutes before a sweep team; they escape together through the city's service tunnels. Beat: reunion as adrenaline—fifteen years compressed into a running start.

chapters.title: What We Buried in Tallinn
chapters.summary: POV Lena. On a night train, they confront their shared past: the operation where Lena followed orders and destroyed Marek's career, believing it was right. Beat: grief and unfinished love.

chapters.title: The Summit Clock
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Five days to the summit. Marek reveals the server contains not just his file but testimony from dozens of burned assets—Karrigan's whole architecture of staged defections. Beat: the stakes become moral, not personal.

chapters.title: Karrigan
chapters.summary: POV Karrigan. The program's architect is introduced at a summit prep briefing: composed, idealistic, genuinely convinced her lies prevent wars. Beat: chilling sympathy for the antagonist.

chapters.title: Ghost Routes
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Using pre-digital tradecraft—paper maps, cash, payphones—they move off-grid toward a contact in Bern. Beat: the pleasure of competence, undercut by exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Bern Contact
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Their contact, a retired archivist named Sofie Brandt, agrees to authenticate the server's testimony—but warns that two of the signatories are already dead. Beat: the cost of delay made concrete.

chapters.title: Sweep
chapters.summary: POV Renner. Karrigan's hunters hit Bern hours after Lena and Marek leave; Sofie covers their trail and is taken in for questioning. Beat: guilt—every step forward costs someone behind them.

chapters.title: The Kill-Box Rehearsal
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Intercepted comms reveal the extraction route was rehearsed with live ammunition. The plan was never to extract Marek; it was to end him publicly and discredit the archive. Beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: Renner's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Renner. Renner confronts Karrigan about the dead signatories; she offers him promotion and a clean conscience by reframing. He takes neither, and quietly passes Lena a warning. Beat: a good man choosing a side.

chapters.title: Interlude: Fifteen Years of Rules
chapters.summary: POV Lena, reflective. Waiting in a mountain chapel, Lena audits her life: every rule she followed, every person it cost. Beat: the theme crystallizes—rules rewritten by power were never rules at all.

chapters.title: The Second Server
chapters.summary: POV both. Sofie's dead-drop reaches them: the testimony is mirrored, but the mirror requires a key—Marek's original voiceprint, recorded the night Lena betrayed him. Beat: the past as the only key to the future.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Pass
chapters.summary: POV Marek. A mercenary team boxes them in a mountain pass; Lena's improvised counter-surveillance buys an escape but gets them both injured. Beat: love expressed as tactical trust.

chapters.title: Karrigan's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Karrigan. Karrigan contacts Lena directly: walk away, and Marek lives; stay, and both are disavowed deaths. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Lie Lena Believes
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena nearly takes the deal, believing she's the poison in Marek's life. Marek dismantles it: Karrigan needs her doubt more than her absence. Beat: the relationship's central repair.

chapters.title: Geneva, Day One
chapters.summary: POV Marek. They enter Geneva under summit security, hidden in a medical supply convoy arranged by Renner. Beat: the trap closing as the city fills with delegations and cameras.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: POV Lena. They reach the physical archive beneath the data vault and find the testimony intact—but the room is wired to alert Karrigan the moment the key is used. Beat: a door that opens only once.

chapters.title: Renner Exposed
chapters.summary: POV Renner. Karrigan discovers Renner's private copy; he's arrested, but not before transmitting the archive's location to three journalists. Beat: sacrifice without spectacle.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV both, alternating. Marek records his key while Lena watches the alarm network. In the recording he says her name. Beat: confession as cryptography—love encoded into evidence.

chapters.title: Everything at Once
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The alarm triggers; the vault seals; hunters converge. They split: Marek carries the testimony, Lena stays behind to hold the door. Beat: duty and love inverted—she stays so he can leave.

chapters.title: What Karrigan Built
chapters.summary: POV Karrigan. Karrigan, holding Lena, explains her philosophy: staged defections as diplomacy's shock absorber, wars prevented by managed lies. Beat: the antagonist's argument at its most seductive.

chapters.title: The Counter-Argument
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena answers not with rhetoric but with names—Sofie, Renner, the dead signatories—people, not assets. Karrigan hesitates one crucial second. Beat: moral climax in dialogue.

chapters.title: Summit Morning
chapters.summary: POV Marek. As delegates convene, Marek reaches the summit's media center with the archive, guided by Renner's journalist contacts. Beat: breathless approach to the point of no return.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Marek. The testimony goes live across the summit's open channel: forty voices of burned assets, Karrigan's signature on each. Beat: catharsis—the truth as an act of force.

chapters.title: The Extraction of Geneva
chapters.summary: POV Lena. In the chaos, Lena turns Karrigan's own extraction protocol against her, walking her out as a detainee into the arriving press. Beat: reversal—the extractor extracted.

chapters.title: Aftermath: The Hearing
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Testifying before an emergency review, Lena refuses to soften: she names every agency that rewrote rules to suit power. Beat: vindication that feels more like accounting than triumph.

chapters.title: Sofie and Renner
chapters.summary: POV Renner, released. Renner and Sofie compare scars over coffee; neither will return to service. Beat: quiet solidarity of the used.

chapters.title: What the Archive Couldn't Hold
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Marek finds his own file: the photo of Lena, logged as a vulnerability. He keeps it. Beat: the private thing the public record missed.

chapters.title: The Question of Staying
chapters.summary: POV Lena. With the program dismantled, agencies offer Lena rehabilitation and rank. She realizes the offer is another rewrite. Beat: the choice the whole book has been building.

chapters.title: No Forwarding Address
chapters.summary: POV both, alternating. Lena and Marek decline everything, burn their operational identities, and leave Geneva separately to meet again unobserved. Beat: freedom as tradecraft.

chapters.title: A Small Country Town
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Months later, a coastal town in Portugal; Lena learns to be a person without a file. Beat: the strangeness and sweetness of an unwitnessed life.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Marek arrives, using a new voiceprint to open nothing but their front door—a deliberate echo of the book's opening. Beat: the motif resolved into intimacy.

chapters.title: Rules of Their Own
chapters.summary: POV both. On the terrace, they write down the only rules they'll keep—three lines, none about duty. Final beat: love against duty resolved as love after duty, with the world slightly repaired and the two of them finally off the books.
